question: What is the correct first-party remote-copy eligibility and request-preparation boundary for directly obtaining Ji Shuying chapter 9 from the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Library holding, and can the chapter page range currently be closed from public sources?
answer: Tokyo Metropolitan Library first-party rules do not limit all remote copying absolutely to Tokyo residents/workers/students. Those users are the normal eligible group; applicants outside Tokyo may also apply for materials not held by the National Diet Library when the material satisfies the library's other requirements. The exact NDL Search record for this 2009 book displays only the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Library under nationwide holdings and does not display an NDL holding, but final remote-copy eligibility remains subject to Tokyo Metropolitan Library's own determination. The chapter-9 page range has not been closed from reviewed public sources; the library explicitly instructs users to use reference service first when the desired pages are not known.

rules: Remote copying is available by postal paper copy and PDF transmission.
Copyright-law scope is generally no more than one half of a work.
People outside Tokyo may be accepted only for qualifying material not held by the National Diet Library.
